item.content:encoded: Golf has officially reached a new high-water mark. And this time, Tiger Woods isn't the only reason. More Americans are playing golf than at any point in history. But the game's latest surge isn't just happening on the golf course. It's happening in garages, sports bars, indoor simulators and entertainment venues across the country. An estimated 30.8 million Americans played golf on a traditional golf course in 2026, according to research from the National Golf Foundation (NGF). That's an increase of 1.7 million players over the previous year and enough to surpass the sport's previous record of 30.6 million, established in 2003 during the height of the Tiger phenomenon. Think about that for a moment. More than two decades after Woods helped transform golf into a mainstream sporting obsession, the game has reached another milestone. Only this time, it has done so under a very different set of circumstances. The 1.7 million net increase represents the second-largest one-year gain in golf participation on record. Since 2019, before the pandemic fundamentally changed how Americans spent their leisure time, the number of on-course golfers has climbed by 6.5 million, a remarkable 27 percent increase. Golf isn't simply recovering. It's expanding. And the most interesting part of the story may be where people are playing. The golf landscape of 2026 looks considerably different from the one that existed in 2003. Back then, the United States had more than 2,000 additional golf courses compared with today. The economy was strong, Tiger was dominating the sport, and social media hadn't yet become the all-consuming competitor for people's attention that it is now. Golf had more places to play, but fewer ways to experience the game. Today, the sport is setting participation records despite having fewer traditional golf facilities and competing with an extraordinary range of entertainment options. The game has also become more accessible in ways that would have been difficult to imagine during the original Tiger boom. You no longer need to reserve a tee time, find three playing partners or commit five hours to enjoy golf. You can grab a bucket of balls at a driving range, rent a simulator bay with friends, visit a golf entertainment venue or work on your swing in your own garage. Golf has expanded beyond the fairways, and the numbers tell the story. While traditional golf participation reached an all-time high, off-course golf established a record of its own. An estimated 39.6 million Americans engaged with golf away from traditional courses in 2026, visiting driving ranges, indoor simulator facilities and golf entertainment venues. This category has established a new participation record every year since the NGF began tracking it in 2014. Growth has moderated from the early years, largely because fewer large-scale golf entertainment venues have opened recently. But one segment continues to spread: golf simulators. They're appearing in commercial entertainment facilities, country clubs, public golf courses, private homes and even garages. For some, they're a convenient way to practice. For others, they're an alternative to the traditional golf experience. And for an increasing number of people, they're simply a fun way to spend an evening with friends. That audience barely existed during the 2003 participation peak. At the time, off-course golf largely meant hitting balls at a driving range. The NGF estimates that only 5 million to 6 million Americans participated exclusively in range-based golf. Today, the off-course universe is nearly eight times larger. The definition of a golfer has also changed, and so has the business of golf. Perhaps the most revealing development is the growing number of people who participate in both versions of the game. They're known as the "Dualies." These are golfers who enjoy traditional green-grass golf but also participate in off-course golf activities. More than two-thirds of all on-course golfers now fall into this category. Their numbers have increased 42 percent since 2019 and 11 percent since 2024. That's an important distinction because Dualies aren't simply casual visitors who occasionally pick up a club. They're among the most engaged participants in the sport. Compared with other golfers, they play more frequently and spend more money on the game. In other words, they're helping fuel both sides of the golf economy. The traditional golf course remains the centerpiece of the sport, but the simulator, driving range and entertainment venue are increasingly becoming part of the same golf-centric lifestyle. And that's a significant shift for an industry that historically defined participation almost exclusively by rounds played on a golf course. Add traditional and off-course participation together, and the numbers become even more impressive. A combined 49.5 million Americans participated in golf in 2026, another all-time high. That's nearly 50 million people engaging with the game in one form or another. It's also a much broader audience than the one that existed during the Tiger Woods boom. Some are dedicated players chasing lower handicaps. Others are occasional golfers who enjoy a weekend round. Some may never set foot on a traditional golf course, preferring the convenience and social atmosphere of a simulator or entertainment venue. But they're all part of the same expanding golf ecosystem. For golf operators, equipment manufacturers, instructors, retailers and developers, that creates opportunities well beyond the traditional tee sheet. It also suggests that the future of the game may depend as much on attracting new participants to alternative golf experiences as it does on getting more people onto traditional courses. The challenge will be converting that enthusiasm into long-term participation while keeping the game accessible, affordable and enjoyable. There was a time when golf's growth seemed tied almost entirely to one extraordinary player. Tiger Woods inspired a generation, brought new attention to the sport and helped propel participation to record levels in 2003. Today, the game has reached an even higher peak without the same singular catalyst. Instead, golf is benefiting from a combination of factors: increased interest in outdoor recreation, pandemic-era participation gains that have endured, technology, entertainment-driven venues and a broader definition of what it means to play the game. The traditional round of golf isn't going anywhere. If anything, the record 30.8 million on-course participants demonstrate that its appeal remains remarkably strong. But golf is no longer confined to 18 holes, a scorecard and a tee time. It's a driving range after work, a simulator on a rainy afternoon, a night out with friends or a weekend round with family. The game has found more ways to fit into people's lives, and millions of Americans have responded. Nearly 50 million participants later, golf has reached a new high-water mark. The remarkable thing isn't just that the sport has broken its record. It's that there are now more ways than ever to be part of it. Golf is booming again. And this time, the entire golf universe is along for the ride. Adam Schupak is a senior writer for Golfweek, covering the PGA Tour. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: More Americans are playing golf than ever before. Here's why

item.title: Reading missing key players for Stockport game
item.description: Reading have played away from home for five matches across all competitions [Shutterstock] Reading head coach Leam Richardson has said he will be without a number of key players for their game against Stockport County on Saturday. The Royals will miss some players because of injury, suspension and international call-ups as they travel away to take on the second-placed Hatters. Richardson's team sit sixth in League One with six wins from 14 games. They beat Peterborough United 5-0 in the FA Cup on Saturday before losing on penalties to Bristol Rovers on Tuesday in the Jersey Mike's Trophy. "[Jacob] Brown is still struggling with his ribs coming off the back of Wednesday [against Oxford]," Richardson told BBC Radio Berkshire. "Jeriel [Dorsett] has been called up to Montserrat but he's had a little knock as well so we'll be without the pair of them at the weekend. "Paudie [O'Connor] is at five [yellow cards] so that'll be him suspended as well - it's a huge [miss] as he's been really consistent and reliable for us. "He's a big personality on the pitch and off the pitch so it's disappointing because I didn't think it was a booking as well on Wednesday night in the Oxford game, but is what it is. "We've got to make sure we overcome, adapt and make sure we prepare as well as possible for these games." Reading will also be without injured defender Josh Knight and midfielder Andy Rinomhota, who Richardson believes will serve his suspension for picking up five yellow cards while on international duty with Zimbabwe. Reading's match at Stockport on Saturday will be their fifth consecutive away game across all competitions, last playing at Select Car Leasing Stadium in late October. Richardson said the club have had to carefully plan their travel and recovery in recent weeks as they played at Plymouth, Oxford, Peterborough, Bristol and now in Greater Manchester this weekend. "We've had to make sure we're diligent with our travelling and everything else with our preparation," he added. "I'm really looking forward to it and think it'd be a really good game. Fingers crossed we're prepared and get a positive result to finish these away days in this block off. "They've been in the play-offs and have been recruiting very well, spending money on different players and always challenged at the top end of this level which is what every club is after. "They're a really good team as well and are well-coached so it'll be a really good game." All the latest Reading news

item.title: No. 10 BYU vs. Baylor: How to watch, listen to or stream Saturday’s matchup
item.description: BYU Cougars players warm up before a football game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News No. 10 BYU (7-2, 4-2) vs. Baylor (6-3, 4-2) Kickoff: Saturday, 1:30 p.m. MST Venue: LaVell Edwards Stadium (capacity: 62,073) TV: Fox Livestream : foxsports.com/live Radio: KSL 1160 AM/102.7 FM/BYU Radio Sirius XM 166 Series: BYU leads, 3-2 The trends For BYU: The Cougars are coming off a painful rivalry loss at Utah, but their College Football Playoff hopes remain alive after only dropping one spot to No. 10 in the latest CFP poll. If BYU wants any shot at playoff action, however, it needs to take care of business down the stretch, starting Saturday against an upstart, inspired Baylor squad. How the Cougars handle the Bears after last week’s letdown will reveal a great deal about their CFP hopes. BYU is scoring 31.0 points per game and allowing 19.8 points per contest, but has not won the turnover battle in more than a month. For Baylor: All appeared lost for the Bears upon firing head coach Dave Aranda in October, but interim Joe Klanderman has managed to rally Baylor for two convincing wins since then to remain in the thick of the Big 12 title chase. Baylor is scoring 31.9 points per game and allowing 17.0 points per game. Quotable BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake walks onto the field for pre-game warmups before a game against Arizona State at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, October 31, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News “We can’t let the Utah loss linger into (this) week, but what we can do is use it as motivation to get better. We appreciate all the fans and everyone who supports us. We know we can play better, and it is my job to get these guys playing at a higher level.” — BYU coach Kalani Sitake “Our margin for error is razor-thin. item.title: Wyndham Clark admits what he really thinks of Jackson Koivun after watching him play at the Presidents Cup
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Wyndham Clark got to witness what Jackson Koivun is really like as a golfer and a person at the Presidents Cup back in September at Medinah. The United States won the Presidents Cup in the end, but the 17-13 scoreline was a lot closer than many predicted prior to the event. Clark struggled for his best form throughout the week at Medinah, but Koivun was one of the stars for Team USA. Jackson Koivun went unbeaten throughout the week at the Presidents Cup , winning two and halving one of his three matches. Wyndham Clark got a first-hand view that week of how the 21-year-old goes about his business both on and off the golf course. And now the two-time US Open winner has opened up on his true feelings about the talented young American. What Wyndham Clark thinks of Jackson Koivun after watching him at the Presidents Cup Koivun is keen to play on the US Ryder Cup team in 2027, and his performance at the Presidents Cup surely means that he is almost guaranteed to be at Adare Manor next year. The 21-year-old obviously has the talent and mentality required to succeed at the very highest level of the game, but what does someone who has already reached that level think about the youngster’s chances of doing exactly that? During an appearance on the Dan on Golf YouTube channel, Clark was asked about Koivun as a player and a person and whether he acts older than his tender years. “ No, he’s a kid, “ Clark insisted. “ I tell you what, I have nothing but praise for that kid. He’s so talented. Obviously, he showed it off at the Presidents Cup. “ You know, a lot of people asked a lot of us what we thought of his pick and I said it somewhere, I was like, ‘He’s our secret weapon’. Because I think, you know, he’s a young kid that has nothing to lose. No pressure, really. “ And then, going up against him as, you know, a seasoned veteran, someone like Si Woo Kim. There is more pressure on Si Woo. “ You don’t want to lose to the kid, right? And sure enough, that’s what happens. So, yeah, nothing but respect for him. “ He is a kid, but I love the kid. He’s awesome. He’s gonna have a lot of success out here. “ That is a seriously glowing reference of Jackson Koivun, and he will surely be very proud indeed when he hears those remarks from Wyndham Clark. It will be fascinating to watch how Koivun performs on the PGA Tour in 2027 with his attempts to make the Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor making for a seriously interesting subplot.

item.title: Red Wings Must End the John Gibson Experiment in Net
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings once led 4-1 against the Florida Panthers on Thursday night. It ended in a 5-4 loss for Detroit. With the loss, the Red Wings have now lost five straight games, but the streak may not be the biggest story. John Gibson is. Gibson stopped 24 of the 29 shots he faced in Florida, and he gave up five goals. That was not a one-night problem. Detroit has played 20 games this season and Gibson has appeared in 13 of them, and he carries a 4-7-1 record with a 3.58 goals-against average and a .862 save percentage , along with zero shutouts. With another bad outing on the pile, it might be time for the Red Wings to finally do something about it. Nov 10, 2026; St. Louis, Missouri, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender John Gibson (36) defends the net against the St. Louis Blues during the second period at Enterprise Center. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Red Wings need to end the John Gibson experiment now The Red Wings are in last place in the Atlantic Division with a 7-10-3 record and 17 points . Detroit has a better chance to win in net right now with Daniil Tarasov, Michal Postava, or Trey Augustine. There is no doubt that Gibson has been a major reason why the Red Wings have been losing. Look, the forward group is not deep by any means. With that being said, Gibson has not played well at all for Detroit this season. Who cares if he has a $6.4 million contract for the remainder of the season. The Red Wings need to seriously consider just scratching him until they can find a trade partner for him, or better yet place him on waivers. Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava would be more beneficial to the team anyways Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava from the Grand Rapids Griffins would be more beneficial to the growth of this hockey team than head coach Todd McLellan continuing to put Gibson between the pipes night in and night out. The Red Wings face the Tampa Bay Lightning on the road on Saturday. If they play Gibson again, this franchise is unserious about its goalie situation and cares more about tanking for a draft pick.

item.title: Four games that matter for Oregon's Big Ten title chances in Week 11
item.description: Having suffered three losses before the calendar flipped to November, the Oregon Ducks find themselves scrapping and clawing to make the Big Ten championship game, hoping to give themselves a shot at the College Football Playoff. It's not an enviable spot to be in, as the Ducks need to receive some help in order to reach the conference title game — but it's the spot that Oregon has put itself in. They've done their part in digging themselves out of a hole, winning two straight must-wins against Northwestern and Ohio State. The wins must continue in the final three regular-season games, home contests against Michigan and Washington and road date with Michigan State. If they don't go 3-0, nothing else matters and the Ducks will be packing their bags for a no-name bowl game in roughly a month. If they don't get some help, and the CFP Committee doesn't deem them worthy of receiving an at-large bid to the 12-team field, that same result will occur. Help is very much needed, and Week 11 is the most important week of them all. Last week, there were ten teams with two or fewer losses in Big Ten play. Now, after Minnesota and Northwestern loss, that number is down to eight. Oregon is joined by five other teams with exactly two conference losses and hoping to be joined by a sixth after Week 11. Tiebreakers will almost certainly come into the picture. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, let's break down the four games that matter towards Oregon's chances of making the Big Ten title game in Week 11, assuming the Ducks take care of business against the Wolverines . The reason this matters for the Ducks is that the Fighting Illini hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after beating the Ducks in Champaign in October, Oregon's third loss of the year and second in conference. If Illinois miraculously wins on Friday night at the Rose Bowl over the undefeated Bruins, Duck fans should worry just a bit, but not too much. The Fighting Illini still have to play Iowa and Northwestern to finish the year. As long as they don't go undefeated, the Ducks will be fine. UCLA is basically a shoo-in as a representative in the Big Ten title game, so them winning on Friday doesn't mean anything for Oregon. item.content:encoded: Having suffered three losses before the calendar flipped to November, the Oregon Ducks find themselves scrapping and clawing to make the Big Ten championship game, hoping to give themselves a shot at the College Football Playoff. It's not an enviable spot to be in, as the Ducks need to receive some help in order to reach the conference title game — but it's the spot that Oregon has put itself in. They've done their part in digging themselves out of a hole, winning two straight must-wins against Northwestern and Ohio State. The wins must continue in the final three regular-season games, home contests against Michigan and Washington and road date with Michigan State. If they don't go 3-0, nothing else matters and the Ducks will be packing their bags for a no-name bowl game in roughly a month. If they don't get some help, and the CFP Committee doesn't deem them worthy of receiving an at-large bid to the 12-team field, that same result will occur. Help is very much needed, and Week 11 is the most important week of them all. Last week, there were ten teams with two or fewer losses in Big Ten play. Now, after Minnesota and Northwestern loss, that number is down to eight. Oregon is joined by five other teams with exactly two conference losses and hoping to be joined by a sixth after Week 11. Tiebreakers will almost certainly come into the picture. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, let's break down the four games that matter towards Oregon's chances of making the Big Ten title game in Week 11, assuming the Ducks take care of business against the Wolverines . Illinois Fighting Illini vs. No. 4 UCLA Bruins (Friday) When: 6:00 p.m. PT | | Friday Where: Rose Bowl | | Pasadena, CA TV: Fox Why it matters: This one's simple: UCLA wins and Illinois is essentially eliminated from the Big Ten title race with their third loss. The reason this matters for the Ducks is that the Fighting Illini hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after beating the Ducks in Champaign in October, Oregon's third loss of the year and second in conference. If Illinois miraculously wins on Friday night at the Rose Bowl over the undefeated Bruins, Duck fans should worry just a bit, but not too much. The Fighting Illini still have to play Iowa and Northwestern to finish the year. As long as they don't go undefeated, the Ducks will be fine. UCLA is basically a shoo-in as a representative in the Big Ten title game, so them winning on Friday doesn't mean anything for Oregon. Wisconsin Badgers @ Maryland Terrapins When: 9:00 a.m. PT Where: SECU Stadium | | College Park, MD TV: FS1 Why it matters: Wisconsin is another squad with two conference losses, and the tiebreaker scenario could get quite complicated. Assuming Oregon wins out, the Ducks and Badgers have the same 2-1 record against common conference opponents. From there, it'd go to the record against the highest-finishing conference opponent, but both teams would've beaten the same common opponents (USC and Michigan State) and lost to the same opponent (UCLA). Then, the tiebreaker would go to the cumulative conference winning percentage of all conference opponents, something that won't be certain until the end of the regular season. To eliminate all of that potential confusion, an upset from the Terrapins would help the Ducks out tremendously. No. 18 USC Trojans vs. No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers When: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Memorial Stadium | | Bloomington, IN TV: CBS Why it matters: This is the biggest one, and it's unfortunate that it's at the same time as Oregon's bout with Michigan. Duck fans, it might be worth rocking the two TV set-up if you're able to, as it holds a ton of weight in terms of the Ducks' Big Ten title chances. The Hoosiers are currently 5-1 in conference. If they win out, they face UCLA in the conference championship. But a loss to USC would knock them down to the two-loss crew and give Oregon the tie-breaker, as the Ducks would have a better record against common opponents thanks to their win over the Trojans. Oregon winning on Saturday is big, but arch-rival USC winning in Bloomington would put the Ducks in the driver's seat for the Big Ten title game. Just this week, Duck fans will have to root hard for the Trojans. Purdue Boilermakers @ Iowa Hawkeyes When: 4:30 p.m. PT Where: Kinnick Stadium | | Iowa City, IA TV: NBC Why it matters: Iowa is in a similar spot as Wisconsin, holding two conference losses with a relatively light remaining schedule of Purdue, Illinois and Nebraska remaining. With the same record against common opponents, the tie-breaker with Oregon (assuming both the Ducks and Hawkeyes win out) would go to the record against the highest common opponent in the standings. That's likely to be Ohio State, a team that Oregon beat and Iowa lost to. But if the Buckeyes crumble down the stretch, that could change and put the Ducks in jeopardy of losing a tie-breaker to Iowa. This would be another miraculous upset, but Purdue getting a win at Kinnick Stadium would further clear the path for Oregon. Contact/Follow @Ducks_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Oregon Ducks news, notes, and opinion s. item.title: What I Want To See From Penn State Vs Minnesota
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 07: Carson Hansen #21 of the Penn State Nittany Lions celebrates his touchdown against the Washington Huskies during the first half at Husky Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Penn State has built a streak of their own, having beaten Purdue soundly and survived at Washington. On paper, the worst is now behind them, and all that stands between the Lions and a “respectable, given where they were at” record is this game. 1) No letup The “second half” problems have been widely documented, and, for all his faults, one thing Matt Campbell has already shown is that it will consider addressing issues within reason. He said as much in his press conference this week, noting that the decision to not go for the jugular at the end of the first half against Washington is something to think about if they’re in that same situation again (reasoning at the time being that momentum was on their side, and they didn’t want to give it up. In other words, conservative). If Penn State finds itself up big on Minnesota, with the ball, and the ability to make the game truly out of reach, I want the game to be truly out of reach. 2) More young’ins Penn State has seen some younger players get extended time as of late. Starting with this game, let’s find out what the future looks like in as many spots as we can. With the exception, of course, of quarterback, where we already know we won’t see Alex Manske unless it’s garbage time.

item.title: As EU grapples with fierce AI competition, summit overshadowed by elusive Ukraine-Russia peace deal
item.description: As EU leaders meet for an AI summit in Dublin, largely overshadowed by Russia's war on Ukraine, William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global. On AI, Pothier points to Europe's limited computing capacity, estimating that it barely represents "5% of what's available out there." Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." Now, turning to the war in Ukraine, Pothier argues that European governments should focus less on "whether they have a place at the table" and more on "making Ukraine's hands stronger," particularly by providing additional air defence interceptors.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Lean Strongly Toward (Kyrie) Irving Staying Put’ – NBA Insider Deals a Blow To Heat, Rockets in Trade Sweepstakes for Mavericks Star
item.description: ‘Lean Strongly Toward (Kyrie) Irving Staying Put’ – NBA Insider Deals a Blow To Heat, Rockets in Trade Sweepstakes for Mavericks Star Amid speculation surrounding Kyrie Irving’s future, The Athletic’s Sam Amick believes that the 34-year-old will likely remain with the Dallas Mavericks through the Feb. 11 trade deadline. The NBA insider made that call Friday, one day after the Mavericks’ blowout loss in Minnesota, even while reporting that rival teams continue to rank Irving first among the players who could reshape the playoff race. Why Insider Sees Kyrie Irving Staying With the Dallas Mavericks Amick built his case around what is working in Dallas rather than around any one suitor. Miami has been reported as a team monitoring Irving, while Houston has also been floated as a possible fit if Dallas ever makes him available. Amick led his latest trade-watch column with Irving, roughly three months before the deadline, and he did not skip past the lopsided result from the night before. “Kyrie Irving may not be traded before the deadline, what with the Mavericks (7-5) looking better than expected and their 34-year-old point guard fitting in so well alongside their young franchise centerpiece, 19-year-old Cooper Flagg.” Amick pointed to the larger sample. By his count, the Mavericks are 7-3 this season when Irving plays and have lost both games he missed. But Amick wrote that the start in Dallas has not changed how rival teams see Irving. “Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact.” READ MORE: ‘It’s So Bad,’ ‘Have You Ever Seen That Drastic of a Drop-off?’ — NBA Champion Urges Knicks To ‘Move On’ From Mikal Bridges After Abysmal 2-Point Night Irving’s contract helps explain why the interest persists. He holds a $42.4 million player option for next season and can become a free agent this summer if he declines it. “The lack of a long-term deal between the Mavs and Irving, all by itself, justifies the outside interest,” Amick wrote. So does his form. Irving missed all of last season after tearing his left ACL in early March 2025, and Amick noted that “the fact that Irving still looks like Irving, after all he has been through, has only added to the intrigue.” Asked about the rumors Monday, Irving told reporters, “I let the team know out of my own mouth that these trade rumors, anything that’s going on with me, do not let this infiltrate our locker room. Don’t let this get in the way of what we have building here.” READ MORE: ‘Why Can’t We Have Nice Things?’ ‘I Just Talked Myself In’ — Bill Simmons Laments Stephen Curry’s Injury Setback Halting Warriors’ Momentum Amick also explained why Dallas wants to get the most out of Irving. The Mavericks do not hav

The Mavericks do not have outright control of their own first-round pick until 2031, which he wrote leaves them “otherwise limited in ways to surround Flagg with talent.” But Amick tied his forecast to how Dallas plays. “Things can always change, of course. But the odds of Irving being traded are likely notably less – if not nonexistent – if these Mavericks manage to play winning basketball,” he wrote. Even a quiet deadline would not settle Irving’s future in Dallas, because his player option leaves the next decision with him this summer. The Mavericks, meanwhile, sit 10th in the Western Conference at 7-5 after Thursday’s loss. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: 'If conditions are flat, watch out': Mike Hesson finds a bizarre way to defend Babar Azam's struggles in Pakistan team
item.description: 'If conditions are flat, watch out': Mike Hesson finds a bizarre way to defend Babar Azam's struggles in Pakistan team originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mike Hesson says Pakistan batter Babar Azam's problems are being exaggerated and blames the conditions. Babar made 50 and 34 in the drawn first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi. He has now gone 42 innings without a Test century. Mike Hesson defends Babar Azam after Rawalpindi Test questions Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has pushed back at the criticism of Babar Azam, arguing that his captain's scores say more about the pitch than about his batting. Hesson spoke after the first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi ended in a draw. He began by dismissing the value of Babar's first-innings fifty, then said the seam movement left any batter at risk. "Look, sometimes, those are condition-dependent. So I don't think the fifty he got in the first innings was a high-quality fifty. And you know, when the ball seams like that, sometimes it's going to have your number on it," Hesson said in a clip posted on X . Mike Hesson on Babar Azam form. 🗣️ "He averages over 50 in Test cricket this year, the highest by anyone who has played 10 innings. If the conditions are flat and he gets himself in, look out." — Sheri. (@CallMeSheri1_) November 13, 2026 Hesson then turned to the numbers and finished with a warning about what happens when Babar gets a flat pitch. "You look at Babar; he averages over 50 in Test cricket this year. It's the highest average for anybody who has played more than 10 innings. So to think he's got an issue is, I think, often overhyped. And I think, as I said, if the conditions are flat and he gets himself in, look out." MORE: India's 89 all-out at Bay Oval a 'trailer' for NZ Test series How did Babar Azam perform in the first Test vs Sri Lanka? Sri Lanka put Pakistan in to bat on a green surface on day one, and four batters reached fifty, two of them on debut. Tayyab Arif made 57 and Mohammad Taha 51, while Babar contributed the 50 his coach has now talked down. Saud Shakeel took it furthest with 93, and Pakistan declared 434 for 9. Sri Lanka answered with 446, with centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis carrying them to a 12-run lead and leaving the match without a clear favorite. Pakistan began the final day 45 ahead and had to bat out the day rather than chase anything. The match ended in the draw everyone expected. Babar made 34 in that second innings, hitting six fours and adding 50 with Shakeel before Milan Rathnayaka set a leg-side trap and had him caught at short square leg. Kamindu Mendis had dropped him on 22. Salman Agha fell to the same plan for 13, and Pakistan finished the weather-hit match on 284 for 8. He missed the opening Test in England through injury, returned at Lord's for scores of 8 and 6, then made 76 and 7 at Edgbaston to finish that series with 97 runs at 24.25. item.title: The 2027 Lockout Preview – Overview
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Derek Jeter talks with Commissioner of Major League Baseball Robert D. Manfred prior to Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 season may not have been great for fans of the Toronto Blue Jays, but for baseball in general, it was a stellar year. While the books aren’t entirely opaque, direct revenue raised by the MLB is estimated at over $13B for the season, the highest ever, and continuing a steady trend line since the COVID shortened 2020 season of about 4-7% growth year over year. Three teams changed ownership this year – Tampa Bay, San Diego, and Los Angeles – selling for $1.7B, $3.9B, and $4B respectively, despite all three facing challenges ranging from the need for a new stadium, a small media market, and a complete overhaul after decades of irrelevance. And yet, despite all of this success, owners are expected to lock out the players on the final minute of December 1 st , 2026. Why would a business that is experiencing runaway success risk everything with the potential loss of games and revenue in 2027? How will the players respond? How certain are we that we’re going to see one side or the other fold and what is at sake for the future? This series will hopefully shed some light on what is often a confusing and opaque process before events start to unfold in real time. Or explain things you already know but give you a dedicated comment section to rail against the players/owners/system/TheMan. The Collective Bargaining Agreement This whole process revolves around the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the MLB and the MLBPA. The CBA remains in force for five years and must be renegotiated after that time. The current CBA expires on Tuesday, December 1 st at 11:59PM which is why the expectation of when the lockout will begin is so precise. The CBA is a wide-ranging agreement which covers extremely consequential things like arbitration, free agency requirements, roster size as well as significantly less important elements like a mandatory chef in each clubhouse. Negotiations for the owners are headed by the MLB Deputy Commissioner Dan Halem and his team and the players are represented by MLBPA Executive Director Bruce Meyer and his team. Halem and MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred communicates with the 30 MLB owners and their specific representatives, and Meyer meets with the Executive Subcommittee and the 30 Team Player Representatives. item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Derek Jeter talks with Commissioner of Major League Baseball Robert D. Manfred prior to Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 season may not have been great for fans of the Toronto Blue Jays, but for baseball in general, it was a stellar year. While the books aren’t entirely opaque, direct revenue raised by the MLB is estimated at over $13B for the season, the highest ever, and continuing a steady trend line since the COVID shortened 2020 season of about 4-7% growth year over year. Three teams changed ownership this year – Tampa Bay, San Diego, and Los Angeles – selling for $1.7B, $3.9B, and $4B respectively, despite all three facing challenges ranging from the need for a new stadium, a small media market, and a complete overhaul after decades of irrelevance. And yet, despite all of this success, owners are expected to lock out the players on the final minute of December 1 st , 2026. Why would a business that is experiencing runaway success risk everything with the potential loss of games and revenue in 2027? How will the players respond? How certain are we that we’re going to see one side or the other fold and what is at sake for the future? This series will hopefully shed some light on what is often a confusing and opaque process before events start to unfold in real time. Or explain things you already know but give you a dedicated comment section to rail against the players/owners/system/TheMan. The Collective Bargaining Agreement This whole process revolves around the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the MLB and the MLBPA. The CBA remains in force for five years and must be renegotiated after that time. The current CBA expires on Tuesday, December 1 st at 11:59PM which is why the expectation of when the lockout will begin is so precise. The CBA is a wide-ranging agreement which covers extremely consequential things like arbitration, free agency requirements, roster size as well as significantly less important elements like a mandatory chef in each clubhouse. Negotiations for the owners are headed by the MLB Deputy Commissioner Dan Halem and his team and the players are represented by MLBPA Executive Director Bruce Meyer and his team. Halem and MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred communicates with the 30 MLB owners and their specific representatives, and Meyer meets with the Executive Subcommittee and the 30 Team Player Representatives. In order to reach a decision, the owners need a 75% majority of votes, so 23 out of 30 owners. The players in theory only need a straight majority out of the 38 votes from the Executive Subcommittee and the Team Player Representatives. For example, in the last CBA negotiations in 2022, the 8 man Executive Subcommittee voted unanimously to reject the owners offer but lost the full vote by the Representatives 26-12. Lockout Versus Strike The terms are often used interchangeably and are both forms of work stoppages but there is a significant difference between the two. Strikes are player led work stoppages during which the players withhold their services. The last MLBPA led strike took place in 1994, specifically to block the implementation of a salary cap, which cancelled the rest of the season and post season and lasted until April 2, 1995. Lockouts are initiated by the owners, which means all player related activities and communications are halted, including trades, signings, training and access to team facilities until the lockout is lifted. The reasoning behind a lockout is that having hard deadlines provides teams leverage in the negotiations, as players will be pressured by not having contracts, job security or access for training and rehab resources to accept a contract more favourable to the owners. What Do They Want? Both sides have been preparing for a potential lockout for the last several years. A series of proposals have gone back and forth between the MLB and the MLBPA, mostly for the sake of media coverage and positioning, as each group looks to bring the public on their side. While the details can shift rapidly, each has outlined a broad agenda of their priorities. MLB Owners Key elements include: Salary Cap and Floor: Tied as a baseline requirement to all league proposals, MLB has proposed a hard salary cap of roughly $258.2 million and a salary floor of $180.2 million, paired with a 50/50 revenue split between owners and players to be implemented in 2028. Shorter Regular Season and Expended Playoffs: Reducing the regular season from 162 to 154 games starting in 2029 to provide a standard weekly off-day and a dedicated Monday broadcast window. Extending the Division Series to best-of-seven and allowing higher-seeded teams to pick their opponents. Roster & Offseason Changes: Weekly roster-setting windows, a 14-pitcher limit, Rule 5 draft adjustments, a reduced draft of 12 rounds excluding high school players, an international draft and an offseason transaction calendar featuring a winter quiet/frozen period. Free Agency and Wages: Increasing the minimum salary to $1M and decreasing the service time requirements from 6 to 5 years before qualifying for free agency. The key for the owners is that they are willing to offer all kinds of incentives for the players; things that are good for them like a year less of team control, having a day off every week built into the calendar, making it more likely good teams have deeper playoff runs, and increasing their potential post season earnings. However, the two red lights for the players are the glaring blaring siren of a salary cap, and the reduction in the draft allowing them to further shrink their farm systems without losing competitive balance with other teams. MLBPA Key elements include: Tax on Low-Spending Teams: A “competitive-integrity tax” targeting low-spending clubs (mirroring the luxury tax for high spenders). Higher Thresholds & Salaries: Raising the base Competitive Balance Tax (CBT) threshold to $300 million (up from $244 million), near-doubling player minimum salaries, and increasing local television revenue sharing. Also Expanding active rosters from 26 to 28 players for the first 15 days of the season. Reduced Service Time: allowing players over thirty to reach FA after 5 years. The key for the players is challenging the disparity in team payrolls in a way that doesn’t limit player earning potentials that a cap would, while expanding financial opportunities for younger players and players who earn MLB spots later in their careers. While the players proposal is more of a wish list, it is wrapped around one absolutely unshakable point, which is that the MLBPA will not consider a salary cap under any circumstances. While the Commissioner and his office have been trying to sell the cap and floor to the players by pointing out the proposed cap and floor would cost 8 teams about $580M in payroll, but it would compel 12 teams to raise their payrolls a little over $615M. While things will develop very quickly, the starting positions by both sides couldn’t be further apart. It also isn’t helped by the complete lack of trust in the MLB owners by the MLBPA. They have resisted every effort for any kind of consistent transparency in their revenue or financial situations, so the MLBPA rejects the owners position that small market teams are uncompetitive and there’s no other mechanism but a cap to re-establish parity. As Paul Beeston famously said: “Anyone who quotes profits of a baseball club is missing the point. Under generally accepted accounting principles, I can turn a $4 million profit into a $2 million loss, and I can get every national accounting firm to agree with me.” Even if the cap is tied directly to a 50/50 revenue split, there is absolutely no

item.title: In Disappointing and Injury-Riddled Season, Shohei Ohtani Finishes Second to Pete Crow-Armstrong in MVP Race
item.description: Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the fifth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Un… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Los Ángeles Dodgers’ four-time Most Valuable Player Shohei Ohtani did not win a fifth award. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did , and deservedly so. Ohtani, who has two trophies from each league, finished in second place. It is the first time in four years that the baseball unicorn has not won the award, but it wasn’t for lack of effort. However, injuries played a huge part in his downfall. As a result, Armstrong filled the void and did an outstanding job, completing a 40/40 season. Shohei Ohtani is One of One The only player to have won more MVPs than Shohei Ohtani is Barry Bonds , who owns seven. For a while, it looked like Ohtani was making another run at history. At the end of June, Ohtani had close to 30 home runs and was hitting close to a .300 average. He was the threat that every pitcher dreads at the top of the lineup. But that wasn’t all; he maintained a 2.00 Earned Run Average as a starter in the Los Angeles rotation and was near the top of the league in inducing strikeouts. There hasn’t been a two-way player with that resume since Babe Ruth. Sep 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) bats as St. Louis Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal (13) and home plate home plate umpire Alex MacKay (9) watch at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Nightmare Finish It all fell apart at the beginning of July, when Ohtani was forced to opt out of the All-Star Game due to a sore knee. The injury persisted, and the consequences were most visible at the plate. After July 1, Ohtani barely stayed above a .200 batting average, driving in fewer than 20 runs, and only hit two home runs the rest of the season. It was obvious that he couldn’t drive off his back leg. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Moreover, Ohtani was swinging at fastballs he usually drives over 400 feet, and nearly every swing drew a shake of the arm or a wince of pain. In short, Ohtani was a shell of himself, even after a stint on the 15-day Injured List. Thus, winning awards. or, for that matter, a World Series was out of the question. The Last Word The loss of a chance at a fifth MVP should be a cautionary tale for both Ohtani and the Dodgers. The lack of communication regarding the condition of the superstar’s health is troubling. The insistence on throwing bullpen sessions after the knee issue popped up is downright baffling

Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did , and deservedly so. Ohtani, who has two trophies from each league, finished in second place. It is the first time in four years that the baseball unicorn has not won the award, but it wasn’t for lack of effort. However, injuries played a huge part in his downfall. As a result, Armstrong filled the void and did an outstanding job, completing a 40/40 season. Shohei Ohtani is One of One The only player to have won more MVPs than Shohei Ohtani is Barry Bonds , who owns seven. For a while, it looked like Ohtani was making another run at history. At the end of June, Ohtani had close to 30 home runs and was hitting close to a .300 average. He was the threat that every pitcher dreads at the top of the lineup. But that wasn’t all; he maintained a 2.00 Earned Run Average as a starter in the Los Angeles rotation and was near the top of the league in inducing strikeouts. There hasn’t been a two-way player with that resume since Babe Ruth. Sep 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) bats as St. Louis Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal (13) and home plate home plate umpire Alex MacKay (9) watch at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Nightmare Finish It all fell apart at the beginning of July, when Ohtani was forced to opt out of the All-Star Game due to a sore knee. The injury persisted, and the consequences were most visible at the plate. After July 1, Ohtani barely stayed above a .200 batting average, driving in fewer than 20 runs, and only hit two home runs the rest of the season. It was obvious that he couldn’t drive off his back leg. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Moreover, Ohtani was swinging at fastballs he usually drives over 400 feet, and nearly every swing drew a shake of the arm or a wince of pain. In short, Ohtani was a shell of himself, even after a stint on the 15-day Injured List. Thus, winning awards. or, for that matter, a World Series was out of the question. The Last Word The loss of a chance at a fifth MVP should be a cautionary tale for both Ohtani and the Dodgers. The lack of communication regarding the condition of the superstar’s health is troubling. The insistence on throwing bullpen sessions after the knee issue popped up is downright baffling, particularly because both parties admitted that it was the act of throwing on the mound that caused the injury in the first place. It not only cost Ohtani the MVP but may have cost the Dodgers a chance at a three-peat as well. Going forward, discretion should be the better part of valor, even if the upcoming season appears to be abbreviated. Ohtani has already etched his name among the greatest players ever to grace the baseball diamond. But going forward, the Dodgers have to make a better effort to preserve the health of their superstar so that he can keep pursuing not only prestigious individual awards but more World Series rings. They have already seen the consequences i f they don’t put limitations on their Superman; he serves as his own Kryptonite. It doesn’t help his team either. President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman has said that “surgery is not on the table” for Baseball’s unicorn. That’s good news. However, the Dodgers are left to wonder what could have been, had Ohtani been more open about his physical well-being. Andrew Friedman said surgery is “not on the table” for Shohei Ohtani. Said it was “whack a mole” between the knee, then the biceps throughout the year. Friedman: “I fully expect him to pitch next year.” — Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) October 21, 2026 Crow-Armstrong deserves the MVP Award. He had an outstanding year, and his 40/40 season put the rest of the league on notice of what one can do when healthy. The earlier Ohtani learns that, the better it is for him…and the Dodgers. Main Photo Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images More Baseball News: Braves Sign Reliever Evan Phillips to Three-Year Deal Report: Veteran Closer Pagán Signs with Tigers Four Critical Needs the Dodgers Have To Address Before 2027

item.title: Patriots vs. Lions Friday injury report: Rhamondre Stevenson, A.J. Brown headline nine questionable
item.description: Foxborough, MA - October 18: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown warms up before the game. The New England Patriots played the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The light will be left on for running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown. Both starters stand among the New England Patriots’ nine questionable to face the Detroit Lions in Germany. Both logged back-to-back limited practices at the FC Bayern Munich training ground while working back from knee injuries. Fullback Reggie Gilliam, tight end Cameron Latu, offensive linemen Walter Rouse and Greg Van Roten, cornerback Charles Woods, and safeties Kevin Byard III and Brenden Schoolers also carry game designations for head coach Mike Vrabel’s side of the aisle. Here’s the final injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. OUT Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) G Ben Brown (knee — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) Lions C Cade Mays (ankle) CB D.J. Reed (hip) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) The Patriots ruled out three prior to the overseas flight. Henderson will be missing his third consecutive game in the backfield due to an illness . In addition to the No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, New England will also go without starters at left guard and cornerback due to knee injuries that arose during last weekend’s 45-27 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium. As for head coach Dan Campbell’s contingent, the Lions also previously ruled out three. QUESTIONABLE Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) TE Cameron Latu (back) G Walter Rouse (concussion) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) CB Charles Woods (hamstring) S Kevin Byard III (chest) S Brenden Schooler (hamstring) Lions RB Sione Vaki (ankle) WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) After sitting out Wednesday’s walkthrough back in Foxborough, Stevenson made the trip to Munich. That was the case for the lead running back despite reportedly facing a multiweek absence because of a knee tendon issue. He’s ahead of schedule amid a season that has brought 128 combined carries and catches along with 657 yards and four touchdowns from scrimmage. Brown, meanwhile, has been listed as a partial participant for three straight sessions. After landing on injured reserve in September due to a high ankle sprain, the June trade acquisition out wide missed the past two weeks worth of practices and starts because of a flared-up knee. The three-time Pro Bowler and All-Pro has caught nine receptions for 101 yards thus far into his Patriots stay. New England also has a pair of candidates to return from injured reserve before Saturday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline for moves. And an open spot on the 53-man roster. New England also has a pair of candidates to return from injured reserve before Saturday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline for moves. And an open spot on the 53-man roster. Van Roten, a veteran of 147 NFL games along the offensive line, had his 21-day practice window open last week after going on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury . An upgrade to full participation has followed while a fellow Patriots guard graduates through the league’s concussion protocol. And at fullback, Gilliam, who arrived on a three-year deal in March, was designated to return from a knee injury before the flight across the Atlantic Ocean. But captains in quarterback Drake Maye, tight end Hunter Henry and offensive tackle Morgan Moses will officially go without game designations.

item.title: 'I knew girls' wrestling would explode' says Skylar Grote
item.description: Skylar Grote knows all about the challenges young girls face in the sport of wrestling. That's because she’s been in their wrestling shoes. One of the Garden State's pioneers in female wrestling, Grote talked about her experiences on and off the mat during a presentation to present and future grapplers at Audubon High School on Thursday. “There’s been a lot of opportunities for these young girls in the sport lately and those are only increasing,” said Grote, who was the 2022 U.S. Open and Senior Pan American champion and placed fifth at the U.S. Olympic Trails in 2024. “I knew wrestling would explode at some point for girls. It’s cool to see a sport that teaches you so much being offered for both genders now.” Grote, the youngest of seven siblings, was introduced to wrestling at an early age and started competing when she was eight years old. Her father, Dr. Walter Grote, was a standout at Cornell University and was an alternate for the United States freestyle team in the 1976 Olympic Games. The Scotch Plains High School graduate was inducted into the New Jersey Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in in 2023. Skylar Grote quickly learned that some of her toughest opponents in wrestling weren’t just the one across from her on the mat, but the people who felt that she shouldn’t be in a singlet and competing. She was the only girl on her elementary school team and, later, the only female on the vaunted Blair Academy wrestling team. “It was really hard at first,” Grote, now 28, said. “There were adults who against me and even some of my own teammates were against me.” Audubon junior Peyton Brining can relate to being the only female wrestler on a boys’ team. It wasn’t long ago that the Green Wave star was in a similar situation. “It was nice to hear someone who is a really good role model talk about a not-so-great experience about being the only girl on an all-boys team and how she turned it into a positive experience,” said Brining, who placed fifth in the state last winter. Girls’ wrestling has exploded in New Jersey since becoming an official sport in the 2018-19 season. Fewer than 500 girls competed in the inaugural season; that number has grown to nearly 3,000 according to data from the National Federation of High Schools. At Audubon, girls’ head coach Bill Scully said he’s expecting eight or nine wrestlers to compete this season, up from three last winter, and there’s plenty of interest in the middle school program, too. Grote explained how her outlook in wrestling, and in life, changed when she stopped listening to negative voices – including the one in her own mind. “For a large majority of my life, there was a negative voice in my head,” Grote said. “Changing that voice and becoming more positive has drastically changed the quality of my life. “Also being able to manage my emotions without taking on everyone else’s was important, too. item.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
item.description: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments

item.title: San Joaquin County girls volleyball CIF State quarterfinal scores, recap
item.description: The first round couldn't have gone much better. All four San Joaquin County girls volleyball teams won their CIF State playoff openers Tuesday, Nov. 10 . Two days later, the road got tougher . Only two of those four teams survived the quarterfinals Thursday, Nov. 12, keeping their state championship hopes alive. Here's how each team fared, along with the scores and a full recap. Division II No. 1 St. Mary's 3, No. 8 Harbor 2 The lower the division number, the tougher the competition and the less separation there seems to be between seeds. St. Mary's is finding that out the hard way. Two days after being pushed to five sets by No. 16 Cardinal Newman , the top-seeded Rams needed another comeback to defeat No. 8 Harbor, the Santa Cruz Coast Athletic League champion and Central Coast Section Division III title winner. St. Mary's dropped the first and third sets before rallying for a 21-25, 25-18, 20-25, 25-16, 15-12 victory . According to MaxPreps, the Rams are ranked No. 73 in California, while Harbor sits just seven spots behind at No. 80. For a closer look at how St. Mary's survived, read The Record's full game story. Division III No. 3 Ripon 3, No. 6 Bullard 0 It's hard to believe a program could reach four straight CIF Sac-Joaquin Section championship games, win two of them and advance to the state tournament each year without winning a single state playoff match. Yet that was Ripon's reality over the previous four seasons. After the Indians fell in this year's CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division III championship , coach Gregory Soliz encouraged his players to turn that disappointment into something more. "Not a lot of teams can get to this point, and they did. At the same time, they're not happy about it I told them, let it hurt. Embrace the hurt. Then get ready for state." Apparently, his message got through. Ripon secured its second straight state tournament victory with a 25-15, 25-14, 25-15 sweep of Bullard, the County/Metro League runner-up. Setter Alayna Sprinkle recorded 31 assists and three kills, opposite and right-side hitter Jorie Eskes finished with 12 kills, and outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11. Outside hitter Ashlyn Malone made her presence felt with 10 kills, 11 digs and seven aces. Division IV No. 3 Santa Cruz 3, No. 6 Ripon Christian 1 If there was ever a reminder of how slim the margins can be in the state tournament, Ripon Christian's nearly 100-mile trip to Santa Cruz provided one. The Knights took the opening set 25-23 against the Santa Cruz Coast League and Central Coast Section Division III runner-up, only to drop the next two by identical 25-23 scores before falling 25-18 in the fourth. Santa Cruz entered ranked No. 177 in California by MaxPreps compared with Ripon Christian at No. 337, but the Knights made the matchup much closer than those rankings suggested. Opposite hitter Alyssa Hofman had 17 kills, two blocks, 10 service points, three aces and 16 digs, while setter Rhian Heuvel added 22 assists and 18 digs. Libe

Senior setter Aniston Hunt finished with 25 assists, six digs, two kills, a block and an ace. item.title: Kevin De Bruyne hails ‘amazing’ Real Madrid star: ‘We based our game plan around him’
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne hails ‘amazing’ Real Madrid star: ‘We based our game plan around him’ Napoli and Belgium star Kevin De Bruyne has this week moved to reveal his appreciation for the talents of Real Madrid starlet Arda Güler. This comes fresh off the pair locking horns on the international front, in a Nations League clash between Türkiye and Belgium. When all was said and done on the evening, it was the latter who secured all three points, courtesy of a comeback 2-1 triumph at The Gürsel Aksel Stadium. But it was youngster Arda who, in defeat, proved himself the star of the show. Continuing what has been a spectacular opening to the new campaign, the 21-year-old took the game by the scruff of the neck, proving himself Türkiye’s leading source of inspiration, and netting a stunning free-kick to open the scoring. Speaking to the media post-match, Kevin De Bruyne was therefore drawn on the name of his fellow midfielder. And the 35-year-old made use of the opportunity to absolutely lavish praise on Arda: ”Arda Güler is amazing. I think his teammates should take more responsibility because all of the responsibility is on him. They should help him. ”We based our plan on Arda. He is one of the best players in the world.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Eight sentenced to jail over Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
item.description: Merab Dvalishvili (left) has won 21 of his 27 professional fights [Getty Images] Eight people have received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday. A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slapping former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind. Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams, with Abu Dhabi police later confirming the incident led to 10 arrests being made. According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi's judicial department, all 10 defendants have been convicted for their part in the brawl. A report by Abu Dhabi news outlet the National went into more detail, adding that six of the defendants were sentenced to six months in prison, fined £62,000 each and ordered to be deported after completing their sentences. It added they have been convicted for "disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives". Two others were given the same punishment, but for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl". The remaining two defendants were fined £10,200 each for "disturbing public security and assaulting others". None of the defendants have yet been named, but Real American Freestyle (RAF) co-founder Chad Bronstein says Dvalishvili has been released from custody. "I'm pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi," Bronstein said in a statement. "We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. "We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us." BBC Sport has asked Abu Dhabi's judicial department for confirmation. Dvalishvili, 35, was scheduled to compete at the RAF event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday against Brazilian Marlon Moraes. Dvalishvili released a video after the incident calling Nurmagomedov, 28, and his team "snakes" as he received treatment on his bloodied face. Nurmagomedov is in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar, who was set to compete against American Urijah Faber at Saturday's event. Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili's teams had a previous altercation at a RAF event in July, which UFC champion Islam Makhachev - a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedovs - suggested led to Wednesday's brawl. Nurmagomedov is the PFL lightweight champion but is out of contract after winning his last bout with the organisation in July. He has been heavily linked with a switch to the UFC but on Friday the promotion's president Dana White said he had not spoken to the Russian. White then called the altercation "ridiculous" and "stupid", and referred to the participants as "a bunch of idiots". item.title: Is Jalen Suggs playing tonight? Magic vs. Bucks injury report
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Is Jalen Suggs playing tonight? Magic vs. Bucks injury report appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Orlando Magic could receive a significant boost ahead of Friday night’s NBA Cup matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks, as guard Jalen Suggs has been upgraded to questionable with a right knee contusion and bone bruise. Orlando’s latest injury report Friday morning listed the 25-year-old as questionable, signaling a potential return after missing the team’s previous eight games. The Magic (4-7) will host the struggling Bucks (1-11) at the Kia Center, with tipoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Suggs last appeared in Orlando’s 111-102 victory over the New York Knicks on Oct. 25. He finished with four points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals across 34 minutes, shooting 2-for-8 from the field and 0-for-3 from beyond the arc. Through three appearances this season, Suggs is averaging eight points, 5.7 assists, five rebounds and two steals while shooting 35.7% from the field and 11.1% from 3-point range in 33.3 minutes per game. His potential return would provide additional backcourt depth for first-year head coach Sean Sweeney, whose team has struggled with injuries throughout the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign. Orlando enters Friday riding a two-game winning streak following Wednesday’s 123-108 victory over the Utah Jazz , which concluded its four-game road trip. Jalen Suggs’ potential return could provide crucial boost for injury-riddled Magic Despite the encouraging update on Suggs, Orlando continues to deal with several notable injuries. Star forward Paolo Banchero remains out with a right high ankle sprain, which has sidelined him since the team’s Oct. 23 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Forward Tristan da Silva is questionable with a left calf strain, while Jamal Cain is also questionable because of a left shoulder contusion. Meanwhile, Jonathan Isaac remains out due to left knee injury management, and Izaiyah Nelson continues recovering from a left ankle injury. Second-year forward Noah Penda is also unavailable with a partially torn right hamstring. With Orlando looking to extend its winning streak to three games, Suggs’ availability could provide a timely boost against Milwaukee. However, his questionable designation does not guarantee that he will play Friday night. The Magic will determine his final status closer to tipoff. Related: Moe Wagner has joking reaction to heated altercation with former Magic coach Jamahl Mosley Related: Magic rumors: Orlando pushing back on rising trade buzz, but something’s gotta give soon

item.title: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’
item.description: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’ Milan sacked Igli Tare in May, but he has broken his silence on why he chose Max Allegri, not getting the chance to speak to owner Gerry Cardinale, and why ‘Christian Pulisic was the biggest disappointment.’ The former Lazio chief was brought in as director of sport, a role that until his arrival had not existed at the club for a while, since the dismissal of Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara in 2023. He did not even last a full year, as Tare was sacked along with coach Allegri, CEO Giorgio Furlani and director Geoffrey Moncada with a single, brutal press statement on May 25. Tare spills beans on Milan experience VERONA, ITALY – APRIL 19: Igli Tare, Sporting Director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and AC Milan at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on April 19, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) “The wound of failing to qualify for the Champions League is still deep, enormous in fact,” Tare told Sky Sport Italia Calcio Unplugged. “If I come to a club like Milan with the target of getting into the Champions League, then I don’t know where I am. This is the most successful club in Italian football history, and after Real Madrid it is the most important in the world.” RedBird patron Cardinale had been an aloof figure at first, but decided after cleaning house that he would take a much more hands-on approach to running the club. “I am disappointed that those leading the club didn’t understand people needed to be given time, something that they are now doing better,” added Tare. PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Igli Tare of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “I’d say you need several transfer market sessions to get a team that is competitive and ready to win. At the start, there was an important responsibility, missing out on Europe altogether and losing the Coppa Italia Final did a lot of damage to morale. “We sold players for a lot of money and signed 10 new figures, so it takes time to integrate, understand and create a united group. We had, albeit in difficult circumstances, been first or second up until the end of March and start of April. In the last 10 rounds, our mentality just collapsed due to other issues that I don’t want to get into, but they did have an effect. “I admit we too deserve some of the blame, because Max and I should’ve paid more attention to certain dynamics, be more present with the squad to get the season over the line.” UDINE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Igli Tare, Sporting director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on September 20, 2025 in Udine, Italy.
